study_id: Yeo et al. - 2025 - Machine Learning for 1-Year Mortality Prediction in Lung Transplant Recipients ISHLT Registry

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult lung transplant recipients using non‑linear AI models (GBM, MLP) to predict 1‑year survival, includes relevant outcomes, and is a peer‑reviewed article published after 2018.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: Institute of Information and Communications Technology Planning and Evaluation (IITP) grant IITP-2025-RS-2023-00254177 and Korean ARPA-H project (KHIDI) grant RS-2024-00512375
identification_methods.Setting: Multi‑center international registry (ISHLT) with external validation at a single Korean hospital
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective study using the ISHLT registry (2009‑2018) and an in‑house dataset (2012‑2024); ethics approval obtained, consent waived
identification_methods.Institution: Transplant Research Center, Pusan National University Yangsan Hospital; Department of Internal Medicine, Pusan National University; Department of Information Convergence Engineering, Pusan National University
identification_methods.Country of Data Origin: International (ISHLT registry) and South Korea (PNUYH dataset)
identification_methods.Dataset Source: ISHLT International Thoracic Organ Transplant Registry and Pusan National University Yangsan Hospital in‑house dataset
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult lung transplant recipients from ISHLT registry; excluded patients <18 y, retransplantation, multiple organ transplants, and those with missing follow‑up or data
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Balanced Random Forest
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Class‑weight adjustments applied for LR, RF, SVM, and BRF models
identification_methods.Comparator: Original 25‑feature model versus refined 10‑feature model; also compared across six ML algorithms
identification_methods.Input Variables: Pre‑transplant clinical variables (25 initially, top 10 most important after SHAP analysis)
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Variables with >20 % missing removed; patients with any remaining missing data excluded (complete‑case analysis)
identification_methods.Validation Method: Five‑fold cross‑validation on ISHLT data and external validation using an independent in‑house dataset
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Feature importance assessed with SHAP values; default model settings without hyper‑parameter tuning; external validation demonstrated generalizability despite dataset differences

population.Inclusion criteria: Lung transplant recipients registered in the ISHLT registry from June 2009 to June 2018, age ≥18 years
population.Exclusion criteria: Patients <18 years, retransplantation, multi-organ transplants, unavailable follow‑up status or missing data
population.Population Notes: External validation performed on an in‑house dataset (216 patients) with compositional differences from the ISHLT cohort
population.Diagnosis: COPD most common (27.9%); other diagnoses include IPF, cystic fibrosis, etc.
population.Pre-transplant Support: ICU admission 6%, ventilator use 3.5%, ECMO use 2.2%
population.Pre-transplant Support Overall: ICU admission 6%, ventilator use 3.5%, ECMO use 2.2%

interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) ranking of feature importance
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Default model settings, no hyperparameter tuning; class weight adjustments for imbalance in LR, RF, SVM, BRF
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is prediction of 1-year mortality after lung transplantation
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: GBM achieved AUC 0.958, accuracy 0.949 on internal validation; external validation AUC 0.852, accuracy 0.764
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Lung transplant recipients in ISHLT registry (n=29,364)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC calculated on average across five-fold cross‑validation held‑out test folds
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: GBM showed highest performance among six models; streamlined model with 10 features retained identical AUC
